title: Speaking Part 2: General Conversation
summary: Every topic in all three themes with the questions you are most likely to be asked, developed model answers, phrases for opinions, examples and the future, and a two-week practice plan.

blocks.text: Part 2 of the Speaking test is the **General conversation**: about **6-7 minutes**, worth **25 marks** (Communication 10 + Knowledge and use of language 5 + Spontaneity and fluency 5 + Pronunciation and intonation 5). It covers the **two themes that were not on your photocard**, with roughly equal time — about three minutes — on each. Your teacher chooses the topics inside each theme and follows up on what you say, so you will not know the exact questions. That is why this page gives you **every topic in all three themes**, the questions you are most likely to hear, and model answers to learn from.

blocks.title: Learn ideas, not speeches
blocks.text: Do not memorise these model answers word for word. Examiners notice recited answers, and they lower your mark for Spontaneity and fluency. Instead, take the **ideas, vocabulary and structures** from each model, then answer in your own words about your own life. Practise with different questions each time.

headers: What it looks like in your answers
rows: Developed answers (Communication)
3-5 sentences for most questions: answer, reason, example (A-R-E).
Narrating events
When asked *Tell me about…* or *What did you do…?*, tell a short story: when, where, who, what happened, how you felt.
Convincing opinions
An opinion + reasons + an example, and sometimes the other side.
Past, present and future (Language)
Every topic: one past event, one present habit, one future plan or *if* sentence.
Natural reactions (Spontaneity)
Respond to what the teacher actually asked; use natural starters like *Well…*, *Actually…*, *To be honest…*
Clear pronunciation and intonation
Steady speed, clear endings (*-ed, -s*), natural rise and fall.

blocks.text: Useful phrases for the conversation

groups.title: Giving opinions
items: In my opinion, … / Personally, I think …
As far as I'm concerned, …
I'm convinced that …
I'd say that … / It seems to me that …
What I like most about … is …
I'm not a big fan of … because …

groups.title: Agreeing and disagreeing
items: I completely agree, because …
That's true, but …
I see your point, but I'm not sure that …
I don't think so, actually.
It depends on …
Yes and no. On the one hand … on the other hand …

groups.title: Giving examples
items: For example, … / For instance, …
Take my cousin, for example: …
A good example of this is …
such as … / like …
I remember once when …
This happened to me last year, when …

groups.title: Buying time
items: Well, let me think …
That's an interesting question.
Hmm, I've never really thought about that, but …
It's hard to say, but I suppose …
How can I put it? …

groups.title: Talking about the past
items: When I was younger, I used to …
Last summer, … / A few years ago, …
The best/worst … I've ever … was …
I'll never forget the time when …
Before I started …, I had never …

groups.title: Talking about the future
items: Next year I'm going to …
I'm planning to … / I'm hoping to …
I'd love to … one day.
If everything goes well, I'll …
In ten years' time, I think I'll be …
If I could …, I would …

blocks.text: Theme 1: Identity and culture · Me, my family, friends and people I know
**Sub-topic: Relationships with family**

items: Tell me about your family. (present)
Who are you closest to in your family, and why? (opinion)
What did you do with your family last weekend / during the last holiday? (past)
Do you get on well with your parents? Do you ever argue? (present / opinion)
How is your family life different from your grandparents' when they were young? (past / comparison)
What kind of parent would you like to be in the future? (future / hypothetical)
Should teenagers help with housework? (opinion)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Who are you closest to in your family, and why?
text: I'd say I'm closest to my older brother, Ahmed, even though we're very different. He's calm and organised, while I'm a bit chaotic! The main reason is that he always listens without judging me. For example, when I failed a chemistry test last year, I was too scared to tell my parents, so he helped me explain it and then studied with me every evening. Next year he's going to university in Alexandria, and I'm honestly going to miss him a lot.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Contrast (*even though…*, *while…*) and a clear reason: an explained opinion.
Narrates a past event with detail, then a future reference: all three time frames.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: How is your family life different from your grandparents' when they were young?
text: It's very different. My grandfather grew up in a village with eight brothers and sisters, and they all slept in two rooms. He started working on the farm when he was only twelve, so he left school early. These days, families are smaller and children spend much longer in education. On the other hand, I think my grandparents' generation spent more time together, because there were no phones. If I could change one thing, I'd bring back those long family evenings.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Comparison of past and present with *These days* and *On the other hand*.
Second conditional (*If I could…, I'd…*) adds complex language naturally.

blocks.text: **Sub-topic: Relationships with friends and people I know**

items: Tell me about your best friend. (present)
What makes a good friend, in your opinion? (opinion)
How did you meet your best friend? (past)
What do you and your friends usually do together? (present)
Have you ever had an argument with a friend? What happened? (past)
Is it better to have a lot of friends or a few close friends? (opinion)
Do you think you will stay in touch with your school friends after you leave? (future)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: What makes a good friend, in your opinion?
text: For me, the most important quality is loyalty. A good friend is someone who defends you when you're not there, not someone who only appears when they need something. A sense of humour helps too, because life is more fun with people who make you laugh. My best friend, Omar, is a good example: when I was ill for two weeks in Year 9, he came every day with the homework and the latest football news. I hope we'll stay friends for life.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Definition with relative clauses (*someone who defends you…*).
A specific past example proves the opinion, and a future hope ends the answer.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Is it better to have a lot of friends or a few close friends?
text: Personally, I prefer a few close friends. When I was younger, I tried to be friends with everyone, but I realised that most of those friendships weren't very deep. Now I have three really close friends, and I know I can trust them with anything. Having said that, it's useful to know lots of people, especially when you start university or look for a job. So ideally, I'd like a small circle of close friends and a wide circle of acquaintances.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Clear opinion, a change over time (*When I was younger… Now…*), and the other side (*Having said that…*).
Sophisticated vocabulary: *acquaintances*, *a wide circle*.

blocks.text: Theme 1: Identity and culture · Technology in everyday life
**Sub-topic: Social media**

items: Which social media apps do you use, and what for? (present)
What are the advantages and disadvantages of social media for teenagers? (opinion)
Tell me about something you saw or shared online recently. (past)
Have you ever had a bad experience on social media? (past)
Should there be a minimum age for social media? (opinion)
How do you think social media will change in the future? (future)
If you stopped using social media for a month, how would your life change? (hypothetical)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: What are the advantages and disadvantages of social media for teenagers?
text: There are definitely advantages. It helps us keep in touch with relatives abroad, and you can learn a lot — I've learnt basic photography from tutorials, for example. However, the disadvantages are serious. Many teenagers compare themselves with influencers whose lives look perfect, and that can damage their confidence. There's also the problem of time: last month I checked my screen time and I'd spent four hours a day scrolling! Since then, I've been trying to limit myself to one hour.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Balanced opinion with examples on both sides.
Present perfect continuous (*I've been trying*) and past perfect (*I'd spent*): wide range of tenses.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: If you stopped using social media for a month, how would your life change?
text: Honestly, I think the first week would be really difficult, because I'd keep reaching for my phone without thinking. But after that, I imagine I'd sleep better and have more time for things I enjoy, like reading or playing football. I might feel a bit out of the loop, since my class organises everything in group chats. Actually, I'd like to try it during the summer holidays, when there's less pressure to stay connected.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Sustained hypothetical language (*would, I'd, might*): difficult to do well.
Natural markers (*Honestly*, *Actually*) show spontaneity.

blocks.text: **Sub-topic: Mobile technology**

items: How do you use your mobile phone in a typical day? (present)
When did you get your first phone? How did you feel? (past)
Could you live without your phone? Why / why not? (opinion / hypothetical)
Should phones be allowed in schools? (opinion)
How has mobile technology changed the way people shop or travel? (past / present)
What new technology would you like to have in the future? (future)
Do you think older people find technology difficult? (opinion)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Should phones be allowed in schools?
text: I think phones should be allowed, but only with clear rules. At my school, we have to leave them in our lockers during lessons, and I think that works well, because there are fewer distractions. However, phones can be really useful for learning — last term our biology teacher asked us to photograph plants in the school garden and identify them with an app. So, in my opinion, teachers should decide when phones are used, rather than banning them completely.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: A nuanced opinion (*but only with clear rules*) and a conclusion with *rather than*.
A real past classroom example adds credibility.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: How has mobile technology changed the way people shop or travel?
text: It's changed everything. When my parents were young, they had to queue at the station to buy train tickets, and they used paper maps. Nowadays, my father books everything on his phone in a few minutes. Shopping is completely different too: my mother orders groceries on an app and they arrive within an hour. The only downside is that small local shops are struggling. In the future, I expect we'll pay for everything just by looking at a screen.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Past (*had to queue*) vs present (*Nowadays*) vs future (*I expect we'll*).
Precise vocabulary: *queue, groceries, downside, struggling*.

blocks.text: Theme 1: Identity and culture · Free-time activities
**Sub-topic: Music**

items: What kind of music do you like? (present)
Do you play a musical instrument? Would you like to learn one? (present / future)
Tell me about a concert or musical event you went to. (past)
How important is music in your life? (opinion)
Do you prefer listening to music alone or with friends? (opinion)
How do you think people will listen to music in the future? (future)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: What kind of music do you like?
text: I listen to all sorts, but mostly Arabic pop and some English rock bands that my older cousin introduced me to. I usually listen on the way to school, because it helps me wake up and get in a good mood. My taste has changed a lot, actually. When I was about ten, I only listened to cartoon songs, which is quite embarrassing now! Recently I've started learning the oud, so I'm discovering classical Arabic music as well.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Reason with *because*, a past contrast, and present perfect continuous.
Personal and slightly humorous (*quite embarrassing now!*): sounds spontaneous.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: How important is music in your life?
text: Music is really important to me, probably more than I realise. I have different playlists for different moods: calm music for studying and energetic songs when I go running. Last year, during my exams, I found that quiet instrumental music helped me concentrate much better than silence. I don't think I could ever live without it. In the future I'd love to go to a big music festival abroad, maybe in Jordan or Morocco.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Opinion supported by habit (present) and evidence (past).
Future ambition with *I'd love to*.

blocks.text: **Sub-topic: Cinema and TV**

items: Do you prefer watching films at the cinema or at home? Why? (opinion)
What kind of programmes or series do you watch? (present)
Tell me about the last film you saw. (past)
Has watching TV changed since streaming services appeared? (past / present)
Should parents control what their children watch? (opinion)
If you could make a film, what would it be about? (hypothetical)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Tell me about the last film you saw.
text: Last Thursday I went to the cinema with my friends to see a science-fiction film about a group of astronauts trying to reach a distant planet. To be honest, the story was a bit confusing at first, but the special effects were incredible, especially in the scene where the spaceship gets caught in a storm. We argued about the ending all the way home, because it was so open. I'd definitely recommend it, but only on a big screen.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Clear narration: when, who, what, opinion, reaction.
Relative clause (*the scene where…*) and recommendation language.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Do you prefer watching films at the cinema or at home? Why?
text: It depends on the film. For action or science-fiction films, I prefer the cinema, because the sound and the huge screen make you feel part of the story. But for comedies or series, home is better, since you can pause, eat what you like and it's much cheaper. Last year my family bought a projector, and now we have a film night every Friday. I think that tradition will continue even when I'm at university.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: *It depends* followed by two developed sides: a convincing explained opinion.
Past, present and future references in one short answer.

blocks.text: **Sub-topic: Sport**

items: What sports do you do or watch? (present)
Tell me about an important match or competition you took part in or watched. (past)
Why is sport important for young people? (opinion)
Do you prefer team sports or individual sports? (opinion)
Are famous footballers paid too much? (opinion)
What sport would you like to try in the future? (future)
If your town got a new sports centre, what would you want it to have? (hypothetical)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Tell me about an important match or competition you took part in or watched.
text: Last spring my school basketball team reached the final of an inter-school tournament. We were losing by six points at half-time, and our coach was furious with us. In the second half, though, we started defending as a team, and with ten seconds left I scored the winning basket. I've never felt so proud in my life! We celebrated with pizza afterwards. Next season we're aiming to win the national schools' championship.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Vivid narration with past simple and past continuous (*were losing*).
Emotion (*I've never felt so proud*) and a future aim: fully developed.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Why is sport important for young people?
text: I think sport is essential, not only for physical health but for mental health too. Teenagers spend hours sitting at desks and in front of screens, so sport is often the only real exercise they get. It also teaches you teamwork and how to deal with losing, which is an important life skill. Personally, when I'm stressed about exams, a game of football always clears my head. If I were the head teacher, I'd add an extra PE lesson every week.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: *not only… but… too*: a complex structure.
Personal example and a second conditional to finish.

blocks.text: **Sub-topic: Customs and festivals**

items: What is your favourite festival or celebration? Why? (opinion)
How did you celebrate the last festival in your family? (past)
What traditional food do you eat at festivals? (present)
Are traditions important to you? (opinion)
Have you ever celebrated a festival from another culture? (past)
Do you think young people will keep traditions alive in the future? (future)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: How did you celebrate the last festival in your family?
text: For the last Eid al-Adha, we all went to my grandparents' farm near Mansoura. In the morning, the men went to the prayer together, and then we helped prepare meat to share with poorer neighbours. In the afternoon, my cousins and I organised a football match in the field, and my grandfather was the referee. The best part was the evening, when everyone sat outside and my aunt told funny stories about my father as a child.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: A detailed, chronological story (*In the morning… In the afternoon… the evening*).
Cultural vocabulary used naturally, with relative clause *when everyone sat outside*.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Do you think young people will keep traditions alive in the future?
text: I hope so, but I think traditions will change rather than disappear. For example, my generation probably won't make biscuits at home for Eid like our grandmothers did; we'll buy them. However, the most important part, getting together as a family, will survive, because people need it. Social media might even help, since people share photos of their celebrations with the world. When I have children, I'll definitely teach them our traditions.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Future forms throughout (*will change, won't make, will survive*).
Comparison with the past and a convincing reason.

blocks.text: Theme 2: Local, national, international and global areas of interest · Home, town, neighbourhood and region

items: Describe your home / your neighbourhood. (present)
What do you like and dislike about your town? (opinion)
What is there for young people to do in your area? (present)
How has your area changed in the last few years? (past / present)
Would you prefer to live in the city or the countryside? (opinion / hypothetical)
Where would you like to live in the future? (future)
If you were the mayor of your town, what would you change? (hypothetical)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: How has your area changed in the last few years?
text: My area has changed enormously. When we moved to our new city near Cairo about eight years ago, there were empty plots of land everywhere and only a couple of shops. Since then, they've built a big shopping centre, new schools and a sports club, so it's much more convenient now. Unfortunately, the traffic has become much worse, especially in the mornings. I think in a few years there'll be even more people, so we really need better public transport.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Present perfect for change (*they've built*, *has become*) contrasted with past simple.
Opinion and a future prediction with a reason.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: If you were the mayor of your town, what would you change?
text: If I were the mayor, the first thing I'd do is create more green spaces, because there are very few places where people can walk or relax outside. I'd also build a public library with a study area, since many students don't have a quiet place to revise at home. Finally, I'd improve the buses, so that teenagers could travel safely without their parents driving them everywhere. I think these changes would make the town much friendlier.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Sustained second conditional: exactly the kind of complex language the top band rewards.
Every suggestion has a reason (*because, since, so that*).

blocks.text: Theme 2: Local, national, international and global areas of interest · Social issues
**Sub-topic: Charity and voluntary work**

items: Have you ever done any voluntary work? Tell me about it. (past)
Why do people volunteer? (opinion)
What charities are important in your country? (present)
Should volunteering be compulsory at school? (opinion)
How could young people help in your local community? (hypothetical)
What voluntary work would you like to do in the future? (future)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Have you ever done any voluntary work? Tell me about it.
text: Yes, last summer I volunteered for three weeks at a children's reading club in our local library. Every morning, I read stories to a group of six- and seven-year-olds and helped them with simple English words. At first I was nervous, because I'd never taught anyone before, but the children were so enthusiastic that I soon relaxed. On my last day they made me a card, which I've still got on my desk. I'm definitely going to do it again next summer.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Narration with past perfect (*I'd never taught*) and a result clause (*so enthusiastic that…*).
Feelings and a future intention complete the answer.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Should volunteering be compulsory at school?
text: That's a difficult question. On the one hand, compulsory volunteering would give everyone the chance to discover how rewarding it is, and some students would never try it otherwise. On the other hand, if people are forced to help, they might do it badly or resent it. Personally, I think schools should make it part of the curriculum, but let students choose the kind of volunteering they do. That way, they're more likely to enjoy it and continue.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Balanced argument with *On the one hand… On the other hand…*.
Conditionals and a clear personal conclusion.

blocks.text: **Sub-topic: Healthy and unhealthy living**

items: What do you do to stay healthy? (present)
Describe your diet. Is it healthy? (present / opinion)
Have you changed any unhealthy habits recently? (past / present perfect)
Why do some teenagers have unhealthy lifestyles? (opinion)
How important is sleep for students? (opinion)
What will you do to stay healthy when you are older? (future)
If you could ban one unhealthy product, what would it be? (hypothetical)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Have you changed any unhealthy habits recently?
text: Yes, I have. Until last year I used to drink two or three fizzy drinks a day, and I often had energy drinks before exams. Then my dentist warned me about my teeth, and I also noticed I was sleeping really badly. So I gave them up completely and started drinking water and fresh juice instead. It was hard for the first couple of weeks, but now I don't even miss them, and I've got much more energy in the mornings.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: *used to* for past habits and a clear sequence of events.
Result and present situation (*now I don't even miss them*).

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Why do some teenagers have unhealthy lifestyles?
text: I think there are several reasons. Firstly, fast food is cheap and easy to order on delivery apps, so it's tempting when you're busy studying. Secondly, a lot of teenagers stay up late on their phones, which affects their sleep and energy. And thirdly, there's exam pressure: students often feel they don't have time for sport. In my opinion, schools could help by teaching cooking and making exercise part of every school day.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Ordered reasons (*Firstly, Secondly, thirdly*) with relative and result clauses.
Ends with a constructive suggestion (*schools could help by…*).

blocks.text: Theme 2: Local, national, international and global areas of interest · Global issues
**Sub-topic: The environment**

items: What do you think is the biggest environmental problem today? (opinion)
What do you and your family do to protect the environment? (present)
Have you noticed any changes in the weather or climate where you live? (past / present)
What did your school do recently to help the environment? (past)
Who is responsible for protecting the environment: governments or individuals? (opinion)
How will the environment be different in 50 years? (future)
If you had the power, what law would you introduce to protect the planet? (hypothetical)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: What do you and your family do to protect the environment?
text: We try to do small things every day. We separate plastic bottles and give them to a recycling project in our area, and we always take cloth bags to the supermarket. My father switched to a smaller, more efficient car last year, and we've started turning off the air conditioning when nobody is in the room. I know these are small changes, but I believe that if every family did the same, the difference would be huge.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Present habits, a past change, present perfect, and a conditional conclusion.
Topic vocabulary: *separate, recycling project, efficient, air conditioning*.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Who is responsible for protecting the environment: governments or individuals?
text: I believe it's both, but governments have the greater responsibility. Individuals can recycle or use less water, but only governments can make big changes, like investing in solar energy or improving public transport. Egypt, for example, has built one of the largest solar parks in the world near Aswan, which shows what's possible. Having said that, laws only work if people respect them, so education is just as important.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: A clear position with reasons and a factual example.
*Having said that…* adds a counter-point: a convincing, mature opinion.

blocks.text: **Sub-topic: Poverty**

items: Is poverty a problem in your country or region? (opinion)
What causes poverty, in your opinion? (opinion)
Have you ever done anything to help people in need? (past)
How can young people help to reduce poverty? (opinion / hypothetical)
Should rich countries help poorer countries? (opinion)
Do you think poverty will be reduced in the future? (future)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: What causes poverty, in your opinion?
text: I think the main cause is a lack of education. If people can't read or don't have skills, it's very hard for them to find well-paid jobs, so their children often end up in the same situation. Another cause is unemployment, especially in rural areas where there are few factories or companies. Prices have also risen a lot recently, which makes life harder for families with low incomes. That's why I believe free, good-quality education is the best solution.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Explains cause and effect clearly (*If…, so…*).
Relative clauses and a convincing conclusion (*That's why I believe…*).

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Do you think poverty will be reduced in the future?
text: I'm fairly optimistic. Technology is already helping: for instance, farmers in villages can now check prices on their phones and sell their products directly. More children are going to school than in my parents' generation, too. However, I think it'll take a long time, because problems like climate change might make farming more difficult. If governments and charities work together, I believe we'll see real progress in my lifetime.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Future forms (*it'll take, might make, we'll see*) and a first conditional.
Balanced view with *However* and a supporting example.

blocks.text: Theme 2: Local, national, international and global areas of interest · Travel and tourism

items: Where do you usually go on holiday? (present)
Tell me about the best holiday you have ever had. (past)
Do you prefer holidays by the sea or in a city? Why? (opinion)
What are the advantages and disadvantages of tourism for a country? (opinion)
What would you recommend a tourist to see in your country? (opinion)
Where would you like to travel in the future, and why? (future)
If you had unlimited money, what kind of holiday would you choose? (hypothetical)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Tell me about the best holiday you have ever had.
text: The best holiday I've ever had was a trip to Luxor and Aswan with my family two years ago. We took the overnight train from Cairo, which was an adventure in itself. In Luxor we visited the Valley of the Kings, and I couldn't believe how bright the colours in the tombs still were after thousands of years. In Aswan we sailed on a felucca at sunset. I'd love to go back one day with my own children.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Superlative with present perfect (*The best holiday I've ever had*) then a past narrative.
Specific, vivid details and a future wish at the end.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: What are the advantages and disadvantages of tourism for a country?
text: Tourism brings a lot of benefits. It creates jobs for hotel staff, guides and drivers, and it brings foreign currency into the country. It also helps people from different cultures understand each other. On the other hand, too many tourists can damage historical sites, and some popular beaches become very polluted. In my view, the solution is sustainable tourism, for example limiting the number of visitors to certain tombs and teaching tourists to respect local customs.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Advantages, disadvantages and a solution: a fully developed, convincing opinion.
Topic vocabulary: *foreign currency, historical sites, sustainable tourism*.

blocks.text: Theme 3: Current and future study and employment · My studies

items: What subjects are you studying this year? (present)
What is your favourite subject, and why? (opinion)
Which subject do you find most difficult? How do you deal with it? (present)
Tell me about a project or piece of work you were proud of. (past)
How do you prepare for exams? (present)
Which subjects will be most useful for your future? (future / opinion)
If you could add a new subject to the timetable, what would it be? (hypothetical)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Which subject do you find most difficult? How do you deal with it?
text: Physics is definitely the hardest for me, especially when there are lots of formulas to remember. When I started Year 10, I got quite low marks in the first test, and I felt really discouraged. Since then, I've changed the way I study: I make flashcards for every formula and I practise past-paper questions every weekend. My marks have improved a lot. I'm planning to ask my teacher for extra help before the final exams as well.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Past problem → present perfect change → future plan.
Precise study vocabulary: *formulas, flashcards, past-paper questions*.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: If you could add a new subject to the timetable, what would it be?
text: I'd add a subject about practical life skills, like managing money, cooking and basic first aid. At the moment, we learn a lot of theory, but nobody teaches us how to open a bank account or what to do if someone faints. My older sister told me that when she went to university, she had no idea how to budget, and she ran out of money in the first month! A subject like that would prepare us for real life.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Hypothetical answer with *I'd add…* and *would prepare*.
Reported speech (*my sister told me that…*) adds variety.

blocks.text: Theme 3: Current and future study and employment · Life at school/college

items: Describe your school. (present)
What is a typical school day like for you? (present)
What do you like and dislike about your school? (opinion)
Tell me about a school trip or event you enjoyed. (past)
Do you think school rules are fair? Which rule would you change? (opinion / hypothetical)
What makes a good teacher? (opinion)
How will you remember your school when you leave? (future)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Tell me about a school trip or event you enjoyed.
text: In Year 8 we went on a school trip to the Grand Egyptian Museum, and it was one of the best days I've had at school. We travelled by coach, and a guide showed us the huge statue of Ramses II in the entrance hall. What impressed me most was the Tutankhamun collection, because I'd only seen it in books before. We also had to complete a worksheet in groups, which made it more fun. I'd love to go back with my family.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Narration with a cleft sentence (*What impressed me most was…*).
Past perfect (*I'd only seen it*) and a future wish.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Do you think school rules are fair? Which rule would you change?
text: Most of the rules at my school are fair, for example the rules about respecting teachers and arriving on time, because without them the school would be chaotic. However, I'd change the rule about uniforms in summer. We have to wear long trousers and a jacket even when it's thirty-five degrees outside, which makes it very hard to concentrate. If students could wear polo shirts in hot weather, I think everyone would feel more comfortable and learn better.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Agrees in part, then disagrees with a precise reason: a convincing opinion.
Second conditional with a result (*everyone would feel…*).

blocks.text: Theme 3: Current and future study and employment · Education post-16

items: What are you going to do after your International GCSEs? (future)
Which subjects would you like to study at A level or in the next stage? Why? (future / opinion)
Would you like to go to university? Where? (future)
Would you like to study abroad? What are the advantages and disadvantages? (opinion / hypothetical)
Who helped you decide what to study next? (past)
Is it better to go to university or to start working straight away? (opinion)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: What are you going to do after your International GCSEs?
text: After my International GCSEs, I'm going to stay at my school to do A levels in maths, physics and chemistry, because I want to study engineering at university. I chose these subjects after a long conversation with my careers adviser last term, who explained exactly what universities require. To be honest, I'm a bit worried about the workload, as my cousin told me A levels are much harder. But if I organise my time well, I think I'll cope.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: *going to* for plans and *because* for reasons.
Past event (*I chose… last term*), feelings and a first conditional.

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Would you like to study abroad? What are the advantages and disadvantages?
text: I'd love to study abroad, maybe in Germany, because it has excellent engineering universities. The biggest advantage is independence: you learn to cook, manage money and solve problems on your own. You also meet people from all over the world and improve your languages. The disadvantages are the cost and being far from family. My older brother studied in Canada, and he says he missed home terribly during the first winter. Still, I think the experience would be worth it.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Hypothetical (*I'd love to*, *would be worth it*) with advantages and disadvantages.
Reported experience of a relative adds a real example.

blocks.text: Theme 3: Current and future study and employment · Jobs, career choices and ambitions

items: What job would you like to do in the future? Why? (future / opinion)
Have you ever had a part-time job or done work experience? (past)
What is more important in a job: money or job satisfaction? (opinion)
What jobs do people in your family do? (present)
What skills do you need for your ideal job? (present / opinion)
Would you like to start your own business one day? (hypothetical)
How do you think jobs will change because of technology? (future)

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: Have you ever had a part-time job or done work experience?
text: Yes, last summer I did two weeks of work experience at my uncle's printing company. I mostly helped in the office, answering emails and checking orders, but one day they let me operate a small printing machine, which was exciting. I learnt that working life is much more tiring than school, because you're on your feet all day. It also showed me how important it is to be organised. I'd like to do more work experience next year, maybe at a hospital.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: A narrated experience with what he did and what he learnt.
A future plan at the end, plus a relative clause (*which was exciting*).

blocks.title: Model answer
blocks.task: How do you think jobs will change because of technology?
text: I think technology will change almost every job. Many routine tasks, like checking documents or working in warehouses, will probably be done by computers and robots. That worries me a little, because some people will lose their jobs. On the other hand, new jobs will appear — twenty years ago, nobody had heard of app developers or drone pilots. So I think the most important thing for my generation is to keep learning new skills throughout our careers.
blocks.marks: Top-band quality: Communication 9-10 · Language 5 · Spontaneity & fluency 5
notes: Future predictions with *will* and *probably*, plus a past comparison (*twenty years ago*).
Balanced and convincing, with a clear conclusion.

blocks.text: Two-week speaking practice plan

Practise **15-20 minutes a day**, out loud. Record yourself on a phone (audio only) and listen back. Work with a partner, a parent or a classmate when you can: one asks the questions on this page in a random order, the other answers without notes.

rows: The test format
Read the Speaking overview page. Learn the 40-mark breakdown and the A-R-E method. Answer 3 easy questions (family, school, free time) using A-R-E.
Theme 1: family and friends
Prepare key words for each question above. Answer 5 questions aloud; record and check: did you use past, present and future?
Theme 1: technology
Learn 10 words (e.g. *notifications, screen time, influencer, addiction, privacy*). Answer 4 questions; include one *If…* sentence in each.
Theme 1: free time
Music, cinema, sport, festivals: prepare one past story for each. Tell each story in 45-60 seconds.
Photocard practice
Use a practice card. Follow the 10-minute routine with a timer, then answer all 5 questions aloud.
Theme 2: home town and social issues
Answer questions on your area, volunteering and health. Focus on giving two reasons for every opinion.
Mock conversation 1
Partner asks questions from Themes 1 and 2 for 3 minutes each, following up with *Why? Can you give an example?* Listen back and note three improvements.
Theme 2: global issues and travel
Environment, poverty, tourism: learn 10 topic words. Practise *On the one hand… on the other hand…* in every answer.
Theme 3: studies and school
Answer questions on subjects, exams and school life. Add one past event and one future plan to each.
Theme 3: post-16 and careers
Prepare your real plans: subjects, university, job. Practise explaining **why** with *because, since, so that*.
Pronunciation day
Read your recorded answers back. Practise *th, p/b, v/f*, word stress (*tech-NOL-o-gy, en-VI-ron-ment*) and *-ed* endings.
Spontaneity day
Partner asks unexpected follow-up questions. Answer straight away using a natural filler. No notes at all.
Mock test
Full test: 10 minutes' preparation, photocard 3-4 minutes, then conversation 6-7 minutes on the two other themes. Record it.
Review
Listen to your mock test. Check: developed answers? opinions explained? past/present/future? natural reactions? Fix your three biggest weaknesses.

blocks.title: خطة الأسبوعين باختصار
items: تدرّب يومياً 15-20 دقيقة بصوت عالٍ وسجّل صوتك ثم استمع وصحّح.
خصّص أياماً لكل Theme، ويوماً للنطق، ويوماً للأسئلة المفاجئة، ويوماً لاختبار تجريبي كامل.
في كل إجابة اسأل نفسك: هل أجبت وذكرت السبب والمثال؟ هل استخدمت الماضي والمستقبل؟
